clue.text: Contents of past capital city

indicators.note: contents are what sits inside, so the synonym of past is held within the inner letters of that same word
the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: past as an adverb means at an earlier time, formerly, the same as at that time

explanation.surface: An inventory of a former capital's treasures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'past' does double duty: its inner pair of letters wrap around its own synonym. Phi bends the one-job rule here.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek capital is a capital city, and was one in ancient times too.

clue.text: Daft to discount British forces

indicators.note: to discount something is to leave it out of the reckoning, so the letter goes

parts.note: barmy is British slang for daft or crazy

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a silly idea of ignoring Britain's armed forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to discount' takes B out of BARMY. BARMY is British slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A land military body is the collective forces of a nation on the ground.

clue.text: Sound of activity leading to a new person

parts.note: a busy place gives off a hum, the low sound of activity

explanation.surface: A buzz of activity heralds the arrival of someone new.
explanation.definitionFit: A person is a human being, so the noun is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Below accepting one word suggesting double negative?

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one word holds the other inside

parts.note: nether means lower or below, as in the nether regions
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A grammar quibble: something below takes in a word that implies a double negative.
explanation.definitionFit: The word pairs with nor to deny two things at once, so it hints at a double negative; the question mark flags the loose description.

clue.text: Digital attachments to online correspondence showing shift in character

indicators.note: one character, a single letter, is shifted to another: here M changes to N

parts.note: emails are messages sent over the internet

explanation.surface: Files attached to emails reveal a change in someone's personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' means on the digits (toes), not computing. TO EMAILS has its M changed to N.
explanation.definitionFit: Nails growing on the toes are literally attached to digits, a playful re-reading of computer jargon.

clue.text: Blade removing head from pig

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is removed here

parts.note: a boar is a male or wild pig

explanation.surface: A knife beheads a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blade' suggests a knife, but it is the flat part of a rowing implement.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat end of a rowing pole is called its blade, so the whole implement can be named by that part.

clue.text: A pair of monarchs in part of church in part of Spain

indicators.note: in places the monarchs within the church part

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church
R stands for Rex or Regina, so two monarchs give R twice

explanation.surface: Two kings and queens are seated in a church somewhere in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A former kingdom, now an autonomous region in northern Spain.

clue.text: Pair penning feasible articles about South-East Mediterranean area

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the pair holds the next word inside

parts.note: a pair of ones written as Roman numerals is II
on means possible or feasible, as in 'that's not on'

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the articles go around the compass point

parts.note: AN and A are both indefinite articles
SE is the compass abbreviation for South-East

explanation.surface: Two people write workable pieces about the South-East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feasible' gives ON in the sense 'that's not on'; 'articles' is plural because both AN and A are used.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the arm of the Mediterranean between western Greece and southern Italy.

clue.text: Plants went successfully on board

indicators.note: on, with board, means aboard a ship, so the letters sit inside the steamship abbreviation

parts.note: board as in going on board a vessel: SS, the steamship
colloquially, to go is to urinate, so went can mean peed
well means successfully, as in 'it went well'

explanation.surface: Something went off without a hitch on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went' looks like plain past tense of go, but it is the slang toilet sense. 'on board' is the crossword convention of being inside a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small blue-flowered herbs of the genus Veronica, so the plural names plants.

clue.text: Moody music in edgy place recalled in personal narrative

indicators.note: in puts the music inside the reversed edge
recalled means called back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a rim is an edge, a place on the edge
emo is an emotional, moody style of rock music

explanation.surface: Gloomy songs played somewhere on the margins are remembered in a life story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' reverses the edge word before the music goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An account written from the author's own experience is a personal narrative.

clue.text: Area supporting wine-growing, say, including a bit of Chardonnay

parts.note: pro means in favour of, supporting

indicators.note: including means containing, so the plant holds the letter

parts.note: a vine is an example of a plant growing wine grapes

indicators.note: a bit of a word is here its first letter

explanation.surface: A region that backs viticulture, Chardonnay included.
explanation.definitionFit: A province is an administrative region, an area of a country.

clue.text: Let's try method, coming out on top of a fight

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming out on top of means placed above the following words

parts.note: how means the way or method of doing something
a bout is a boxing match or fight

explanation.surface: A method that wins a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming out on top' suggests winning, but in a down answer it only means placed above.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase proposes an option, as in 'shall we try this?', so it is an idiom for suggesting a trial.

clue.text: Alternatively providing allocation to a different worker

definitions.meaning: an expression introducing a contrasting point

definitions.text: providing allocation to a different worker
definitions.meaning: read literally, placing a task upon another hand, a hand being a worker

explanation.surface: A manager reassigns a job to someone else instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom introduces a contrasting view, exactly what alternatively does in a sentence.

clue.text: Man had tossed coins in the study of pleasure

parts.note: he'd is short for he had, man giving he

indicators.note: tossed coins are flipped and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man had flipped coins, as in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: This branch of psychology deals with pleasant and unpleasant feelings, hence pleasure study.

clue.text: They praise drifting ocean mists

indicators.note: drifting means moving aimlessly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: People admire sea fog rolling in.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers of formal eulogies are those who praise, from encomium, a speech of praise.

clue.text: Nationalist approach to festival right? Not 20 Across

parts.note: the eve is the day before a festival, as with Christmas Eve

explanation.surface: A patriot heads to a festival, asking whether that is right.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 Across is AT ALL, so the definition reads 'Not at all'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'not at all' is a flat denial, the same as saying not ever.

clue.text: Bigwig entertaining bridge team to make sharp form of visual communication

indicators.note: entertaining means having as a guest, so the bigwig holds the team inside

parts.note: a VIP is a very important person, a bigwig
East and West form one partnership at the bridge table
to hone a blade is to sharpen it

explanation.surface: An important person hosts a bridge pair to sharpen up a video link.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a telephone with a screen, letting callers see each other, so visual communication.

clue.text: Person receiving attention dreads variant view

indicators.note: a variant is an altered form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to see is to view

explanation.surface: Someone in the spotlight fears a differing opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attention' belongs to the definition: a letter marked for someone's attention goes to them.
explanation.definitionFit: The one a letter or speech is directed to is its recipient, the person whose attention is sought.

clue.text: Not showing results of attention regarding dress to clothe Queen

parts.note: over can mean about or regarding, as in a dispute over money

indicators.note: to clothe is to cover, so the dress wraps around the letter

parts.note: a gown is a long dress
R is short for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A dresser fusses over what the Queen should wear.
explanation.definitionFit: A neglected garden is overgrown, showing that nobody has tended it.

clue.text: Seize grain and fruit

parts.note: gr is the abbreviation for grain, a small unit of weight
an apple is a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone grabs cereal and fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To grapple with or grab hold of something is to seize it.

clue.text: Article stretching credulity of any kind

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
a tall story is one hard to believe

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece that is hard to believe.
explanation.definitionFit: Used after a negative, the phrase means in any way whatever, as in 'no idea of any kind'.

clue.text: Unanimous about degree being finished

indicators.note: about means around, so the first phrase surrounds the letter

parts.note: all one means united, all of one mind

explanation.surface: Everyone agrees about a degree being completed.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying a task is completely over or done is to say it is finished.

clue.text: One million having run in disrupted capital city? That shows unworkable situation

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A huge sum is spent while the capital is in chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupted' rearranges CAPITAL CITY together with R; the result follows I and M.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of being unfeasible or unworkable is exactly what the abstract noun names.

clue.text: Shabby races held in river

indicators.note: held in means contained within, so the races sit inside the river

parts.note: the Tay is a river in Scotland
TT, Tourist Trophy, is the motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Run-down races taking place on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tay is Scotland's longest river; the TT is the Isle of Man motorbike race.
explanation.definitionFit: Tatty means worn and scruffy, a close synonym of shabby.

clue.text: Examination removing top of reef feature

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, which is taken away

parts.note: reefs are built of coral

explanation.surface: An inspection that strips the surface of a reef.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken test, as in a viva, is an examination given by word of mouth.

clue.text: Playwright initially ready to occupy end apartment

parts.note: to stop is to end

indicators.note: to occupy is to be inside, so the letter goes inside the flat

parts.note: a pad is slang for a flat or apartment

indicators.note: initially means at the start, taking the first letter

explanation.surface: A dramatist is ready to move into a flat at the end of the street.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Stoppard is the British playwright of Arcadia.
explanation.definitionFit: He is a famous British dramatist, so an example of a playwright.

clue.text: Large animal wanting endless space

indicators.note: endless means without its last letter

parts.note: room means space, as in room to move

explanation.surface: A big creature needs limitless space.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for kangaroo, a large Australian marsupial, so an animal.

clue.text: Medic presumably able to give a second opinion?

definitions.text: Medic presumably able to give a second opinion?

parts.words: Medic presumably able to give a second opinion?
parts.note: Stevenson's ... had a second self, Mr Hyde, so he could literally offer a second opinion of his own

explanation.walkthrough: A second opinion is normally from another doctor; this doctor has another personality who might give one.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional physician of Stevenson's tale, whose alter ego is Mr Hyde, is a medic with two minds.

clue.text: 50 involved in clay-pigeon shooting never returning for winter sport

indicators.note: involved in means placed inside the shooting sport

parts.note: skeet is a form of clay-pigeon shooting
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: no can mean never, as in 'no way'

explanation.surface: Fifty people take up clay-pigeon shooting and never come back to the winter sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' puts L in SKEET; 'returning' turns NO into ON.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a head-first sliding sled event at the Winter Olympics.
